When his opponent rushed to the net, he hit a perfect lob that sailed over her head and landed inside the line.
She surprised her opponent with a delicate drop shot that barely cleared the net and stopped just inside the service box.
The coach told him to change his grip slightly in order to add more spin to his forehand.

He played a deep approach shot to the backhand corner and then moved forward to finish with a volley.
She used a slice backhand to keep the ball low and force her opponent to lift it, creating an easy put-away.

stage_2_story.text_en:
It was a quiet Friday evening and Moshe was watching a Wimbledon semifinal on television with his daughter Tamar, who played tennis seriously in her youth and still follows every major tournament.

The match was tense. Both players stayed behind the baseline, exchanging long groundstrokes that pushed each other from corner to corner. Tamar explained to Moshe: 'You see, Aba, both players are baseline specialists. They prefer to win from the back rather than rush the net.'

In the seventh game, the second player earned a break point on the first player's serve. Moshe leaned forward in his chair. The server hit a heavy topspin that landed deep, using the spin to push his opponent behind the baseline. Then he moved in and played a sharp approach shot to the backhand corner. His opponent, now under pressure, tried to pass him with a slice that stayed too low — it clipped the net and the break point was saved.

The match went to a tiebreak. Both players were nervous. Then came the moment Moshe talked about for weeks afterwards. The second player charged the net and looked certain to win the point. But his opponent, standing deep, lifted an incredible lob that arched perfectly over the net player's head and landed just inside the baseline. The crowd erupted.

On the very next point, the first player earned a match point — one point from victory. He stepped up to serve, the crowd fell silent, and he hit a thundering first serve right down the centre. His opponent could barely get his return back. A crisp drop shot finished the point. Match over.

Moshe clapped his hands and said to Tamar: 'Now I understand why you loved this sport so much. Every point is a little battle.' Tamar smiled: 'Exactly, Aba. You see it now.'
